correctness.rationale: For each H≤deck group of a finite connected regular graph covering free on undirected edges without inversion, quotient edge fibers are exact H-orbits. Preimage of a quotient forest is a disjoint union of lifted trees. If the quotient subset has a cyclic non-backtracking closed walk, finite monodromy order gives a closed lift and hence a cycle. Thus orbit-compressed geometric fixed forest complex is exactly the forest complex of quotient X/H. Graphic matroid rank q-1 and shellability give a sphere wedge in degree q-2 with multiplicity T(0,1), empty for q=1. Fixed-point reduced Lefschetz equals (-1)^(q-2)T, while upstairs top homology degree v-2 yields trace (-1)^(v-q)T. Rational orbit invariants follow by averaging; verified graph-cover source checks/verify.py encodes exhaustive edge-orbit subset forests and signed simplex traces for cyclic and Klein-four examples including loops/parallel edges. The Klein-four crown graph example yields top rank 64, three nontrivial traces 4 and quotient rank (64+3*4)/4=19. No universal inference from finite checks.

originality.rationale: Graphic-matroid independence shellability and Tutte sphere counts are classical; Moci–Pezzoli addresses general homological representation under matroid automorphisms, and another complete-graph free action result provides coned-multigraph forest fixed models. Neither gives the universal edge-free regular-cover quotient-forest PL equivalence and every-deck-element signed Tutte character for arbitrary X. The present claim applies to finite regular graph covers with edge-inversion excluded.

value.rationale: A natural functorial identification of fixed spaces with quotient graphic matroid complexes supplies all subgroup homotopy types and the complete rational deck-group character for general finite regular covers. The edge-inversion boundary is mathematically essential; the result is substantially more than a routine Tutte evaluation after a given graph.
